findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_auth_challenge, submit_deposit, submit_withdrawal · Private data: list_pools, get_balances, get_bridge_balances, get_config, get_default_config, get_rewards, get_transaction_costs, get_token_info, get_auth_challenge, submit_auth_verify, prepare_deposit, submit_deposit, get_deposit_status, prepare_withdrawal, submit_withdrawal, prepare_config, submit_config · Public sink: get_rewards, submit_auth_verify, prepare_deposit, submit_deposit, submit_withdrawal, submit_config · Destructive: get_config, prepare_config.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_auth_challenge, submit_deposit, submit_withdrawal · Private data: list_pools, get_balances, get_bridge_balances, get_config, get_default_config, get_rewards, get_transaction_costs, get_token_info, get_auth_challenge, submit_auth_verify, prepare_deposit, submit_deposit, get_deposit_status, prepare_withdrawal, submit_withdrawal, prepare_config, submit_config · Public sink: get_rewards, submit_auth_verify, prepare_deposit, submit_deposit, submit_withdrawal, submit_config · Destructive: get_config, prepare_config

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
